 1	# PeeGeeQ - Getting Started Guide 
 2	#### © Mark Andrew Ray-Smith Cityline Ltd 2025
 3	
 4	Welcome to **PeeGeeQ** (PostgreSQL as a Message Queue) - a production-ready message queue system built on PostgreSQL that provides both high-performance real-time messaging and transactional messaging patterns.
 5	
 6	## What is PeeGeeQ?
 7	
 8	PeeGeeQ is an enterprise-grade message queue system that leverages PostgreSQL's advanced features to provide:
 9	
 10	- **Native Queue**: High-performance, real-time message processing (10,000+ msg/sec, <10ms latency)
 11	- **Outbox Pattern**: Transactional messaging with database consistency guarantees (5,000+ msg/sec)
 12	- **Production Features**: Health checks, metrics, circuit breakers, dead letter queues, and more
 13	
 14	## Architecture Overview
 15	
 16	```mermaid
 17	graph TB
 18	 subgraph "Application Layer"
 19	 APP[Your Application<br/>Producer/Consumer Code]
 20	 end
 21	
 22	 subgraph "PeeGeeQ API Layer"
 23	 API[peegeeq-api<br/>MessageProducer<T><br/>MessageConsumer<T><br/>QueueFactory<br/>QueueFactoryProvider]
 24	 end
 25	
 26	 subgraph "Implementation Layer"
 27	 NATIVE[peegeeq-native<br/>Real-time LISTEN/NOTIFY<br/>10,000+ msg/sec<br/><10ms latency]
 28	 OUTBOX[peegeeq-outbox<br/>Transactional guarantees<br/>5,000+ msg/sec<br/>Polling-based]
 29	 end
 30	
 31	 subgraph "Database Layer"
 32	 DB[peegeeq-db<br/>PeeGeeQManager<br/>Schema Migrations<br/>Health Checks<br/>Metrics<br/>Circuit Breakers<br/>Dead Letter Queue]
 33	 end
 34	
 35	 subgraph "PostgreSQL Database"
 36	 POSTGRES[(PostgreSQL<br/>queue_messages<br/>outbox<br/>dead_letter_queue)]
 37	 end
 38	
 39	 APP --> API
 40	 API --> NATIVE
 41	 API --> OUTBOX
 42	 NATIVE --> DB
 43	 OUTBOX --> DB
 44	 DB --> POSTGRES
 45	```
 46	
 47	## System Requirements
 48	
 49	### Prerequisites
 50	
 51	- **Java**: JDK 21 or higher
 52	- **Maven**: 3.6 or higher
 53	- **Docker**: Required for self-contained demo (recommended for getting started)
 54	- **PostgreSQL**: 15+ (if not using Docker demo)
 55	
 56	### Dependencies
 57	
 58	PeeGeeQ automatically manages these dependencies:
 59	- PostgreSQL JDBC Driver (42.6.0)
 60	- HikariCP Connection Pooling (5.0.1)
 61	- Vert.x Async Framework (4.5.11)
 62	- Jackson JSON Processing (2.15.2)
 63	- Micrometer Metrics (1.12.0)
 64	- Resilience4j Circuit Breakers (2.1.0)
 65	
 66	## Quick Start (Recommended)
 67	
 68	The fastest way to get started is with our self-contained demo that requires no setup:
 69	
 70	### Option 1: Using Shell Scripts
 71	
 72	**Windows:**
 73	```cmd
 74	run-self-contained-demo.bat
 75	```
 76	
 77	**Unix/Linux/macOS:**
 78	```bash
 79	./run-self-contained-demo.sh
 80	```
 81	
 82	### Option 2: Using Maven Directly
 83	
 84	```bash
 85	mvn compile exec:java \
 86	 -Dexec.mainClass="dev.mars.peegeeq.examples.PeeGeeQSelfContainedDemo" \
 87	 -pl peegeeq-examples
 88	```
 89	
 90	This demo will:
 91	- Start a PostgreSQL container automatically
 92	- Demonstrate all PeeGeeQ production features
 93	- Show both Native and Outbox patterns
 94	- Clean up containers when finished
 95	- Require no external setup
 96	
 97	## Installation & Setup
 98	
 99	### 1. Clone the Repository
 100	
 101	```bash
 102	git clone <repository-url>
 103	cd peegeeq
 104	```
 105	
 106	### 2. Build the Project
 107	
 108	```bash
 109	mvn clean compile
 110	```
 111	
 112	### 3. Database Setup (If Not Using Docker Demo)
 113	
 114	#### Option A: Local PostgreSQL
 115	
 116	1. Install PostgreSQL 15+
 117	2. Create database and user:
 118	
 119	```sql
 120	CREATE DATABASE peegeeq;
 121	CREATE USER peegeeq WITH PASSWORD 'peegeeq';
 122	GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON DATABASE peegeeq TO peegeeq;
 123	```
 124	
 125	#### Option B: Docker PostgreSQL
 126	
 127	```bash
 128	docker run -d \
 129	 --name peegeeq-postgres \
 130	 -e POSTGRES_DB=peegeeq \
 131	 -e POSTGRES_USER=peegeeq \
 132	 -e POSTGRES_PASSWORD=peegeeq \
 133	 -p 5432:5432 \
 134	 postgres:15
 135	```
 136	
 137	### 4. Run Traditional Example
 138	
 139	```bash
 140	# With default configuration
 141	java -cp <classpath> dev.mars.peegeeq.examples.PeeGeeQExample
 142	
 143	# With specific profile
 144	java -Dpeegeeq.profile=production -cp <classpath> dev.mars.peegeeq.examples.PeeGeeQExample
 145	```
 146	
 147	## Basic Usage
 148	
 149	### Initialize PeeGeeQ Manager
 150	
 151	```java
 152	import dev.mars.peegeeq.db.PeeGeeQManager;
 153	import dev.mars.peegeeq.db.config.PeeGeeQConfiguration;
 154	import io.micrometer.core.instrument.simple.SimpleMeterRegistry;
 155	
 156	// Initialize with configuration profile
 157	PeeGeeQManager manager = new PeeGeeQManager(
 158	 new PeeGeeQConfiguration("development"), 
 159	 new SimpleMeterRegistry()
 160	);
 161	
 162	// Start all services
 163	manager.start();
 164	```
 165	
 166	### Native Queue - High Performance Real-time
 167	
 168	```java
 169	import dev.mars.peegeeq.api.*;
 170	import dev.mars.peegeeq.db.provider.PgDatabaseService;
 171	import dev.mars.peegeeq.db.provider.PgQueueFactoryProvider;
 172	
 173	// Create database service and factory provider
 174	DatabaseService databaseService = new PgDatabaseService(manager);
 175	QueueFactoryProvider provider = new PgQueueFactoryProvider();
 176	
 177	// Create native queue factory
 178	QueueFactory nativeFactory = provider.createNativeQueueFactory(databaseService);
 179	
 180	// Create producer and consumer
 181	MessageProducer<String> producer = nativeFactory.createProducer("my-topic", String.class);
 182	MessageConsumer<String> consumer = nativeFactory.createConsumer("my-topic", String.class);
 183	
 184	// Send messages
 185	producer.send("Hello, PeeGeeQ!");
 186	
 187	// Consume messages
 188	consumer.consume(message -> {
 189	 System.out.println("Received: " + message.getPayload());
 190	 return true; // Acknowledge message
 191	});
 192	```
 193	
 194	### Outbox Pattern - Transactional Guarantees
 195	
 196	```java
 197	// Create outbox queue factory
 198	QueueFactory outboxFactory = provider.createOutboxQueueFactory(databaseService);
 199	
 200	// Create producer and consumer
 201	MessageProducer<String> outboxProducer = outboxFactory.createProducer("my-outbox-topic", String.class);
 202	MessageConsumer<String> outboxConsumer = outboxFactory.createConsumer("my-outbox-topic", String.class);
 203	
 204	// Send messages with transactional guarantees
 205	outboxProducer.send("Transactional message");
 206	
 207	// Consume messages
 208	outboxConsumer.consume(message -> {
 209	 System.out.println("Received transactional: " + message.getPayload());
 210	 return true;
 211	});
 212	```
 213	
 214	## Configuration
 215	
 216	### Environment Profiles
 217	
 218	PeeGeeQ supports multiple configuration profiles:
 219	
 220	- `development` - Default settings for local development
 221	- `production` - Optimized for production environments
 222	- `test` - Configured for testing scenarios
 223	
 224	### Configuration Files
 225	
 226	Configuration is loaded from:
 227	1. `peegeeq-default.properties` (base configuration)
 228	2. `peegeeq-{profile}.properties` (profile-specific overrides)
 229	3. System properties (highest priority)
 230	4. Environment variables
 231	
 232	### Key Configuration Properties
 233	
 234	```properties
 235	# Database Configuration
 236	peegeeq.database.host=localhost
 237	peegeeq.database.port=5432
 238	peegeeq.database.name=peegeeq
 239	peegeeq.database.username=peegeeq
 240	peegeeq.database.password=peegeeq
 241	
 242	# Connection Pool
 243	peegeeq.database.pool.min-size=5
 244	peegeeq.database.pool.max-size=10
 245	
 246	# Queue Settings
 247	peegeeq.queue.max-retries=3
 248	peegeeq.queue.visibility-timeout=PT30S
 249	peegeeq.queue.dead-letter.enabled=true
 250	
 251	# Metrics & Monitoring
 252	peegeeq.metrics.enabled=true
 253	peegeeq.health.enabled=true
 254	peegeeq.circuit-breaker.enabled=true
 255	```
 256	
 257	## Module Structure
 258	
 259	PeeGeeQ is organized into focused modules:
 260	
 261	- **peegeeq-api**: Core interfaces and contracts
 262	- **peegeeq-db**: Database management, migrations, health checks
 263	- **peegeeq-native**: High-performance LISTEN/NOTIFY implementation
 264	- **peegeeq-outbox**: Transactional outbox pattern implementation
 265	- **peegeeq-examples**: Self-contained demo applications
 266	
 267	## Production Features
 268	
 269	### Health Checks
 270	```java
 271	boolean healthy = manager.isHealthy();
 272	PeeGeeQManager.SystemStatus status = manager.getSystemStatus();
 273	```
 274	
 275	### Metrics Collection
 276	```java
 277	// Metrics are automatically collected and available via Micrometer
 278	// Integrate with Prometheus, Grafana, or other monitoring systems
 279	```
 280	
 281	### Circuit Breakers
 282	```java
 283	// Automatic circuit breaker protection for database operations
 284	// Configurable failure thresholds and recovery timeouts
 285	```
 286	
 287	### Dead Letter Queue
 288	```java
 289	// Failed messages automatically moved to dead letter queue
 290	// Supports message reprocessing and failure analysis
 291	```
 292	
 293	## Next Steps
 294	
 295	1. **Explore the Examples**: Run the self-contained demo to see all features
 296	2. **Read the Documentation**: Check out the `docs/` directory for detailed guides
 297	3. **Run Tests**: Execute `mvn test` to see comprehensive integration tests
 298	4. **Customize Configuration**: Adapt settings for your environment
 299	5. **Integrate with Your Application**: Use PeeGeeQManager in your code
 300	6. **Set up Monitoring**: Configure metrics collection and alerting
 301	
 302	## Troubleshooting
 303	
 304	### Common Issues
 305	
 306	1. **Docker Not Running**
 307	 - Ensure Docker Desktop is started
 308	 - Check `docker info` command works
 309	
 310	2. **Database Connection Failed**
 311	 - Verify PostgreSQL is running
 312	 - Check host, port, and credentials
 313	 - Ensure database exists and user has permissions
 314	
 315	3. **Port Conflicts**
 316	 - Default PostgreSQL port is 5432
 317	 - Change port in configuration if needed
 318	
 319	### Getting Help
 320	
 321	- Check the logs in the `logs/` directory
 322	- Review the comprehensive documentation in `docs/`
 323	- Examine the example code in `peegeeq-examples/`
 324	- Run tests to verify your setup: `mvn test`
 325

 707	
 708	### When to Use Native Queue
 709	- High-throughput, low-latency requirements
 710	- Real-time event processing
 711	- Independent message processing
 712	- When immediate delivery is important
 713	
 714	### When to Use Outbox Pattern
 715	- Transactional consistency requirements
 716	- Integration with existing database transactions
 717	- When message delivery must be guaranteed
 718	- Complex business transactions

 124	
 125	## Key Features
 126	
 127	### 1. Real-time Message Processing
 128	- **LISTEN/NOTIFY**: Immediate message delivery using PostgreSQL's pub/sub
 129	- **Zero Polling**: Messages are pushed to consumers instantly
 130	- **Channel Management**: Automatic channel subscription and cleanup
 131	
 132	### 2. Concurrency Control
 133	- **Advisory Locks**: Prevents duplicate message processing
 134	- **Visibility Timeout**: Automatic message release after timeout
 135	- **Lock Expiration**: Background cleanup of expired locks
 136	
 137	### 3. Reliability & Resilience
 138	- **Dead Letter Queue**: Failed messages moved to DLQ after retry limit
 139	- **Circuit Breakers**: Automatic failure detection and recovery
 140	- **Health Checks**: Continuous system health monitoring
 141	- **Backpressure**: Automatic load management
...
 160	
 161	### Latency
 162	- **Real-time Delivery**: <10ms with LISTEN/NOTIFY
 163	- **Polling-based**: 2-5 seconds (configurable)
 164	- **Processing Overhead**: <1ms per message
 165	
 166	### Scalability
 167	- **Horizontal Scaling**: Multiple consumer instances
 168	- **Vertical Scaling**: Leverages PostgreSQL performance
 169	- **Connection Pooling**: Efficient resource utilization

 1	# PostgreSQL as a Message Queue (PeeGeeQ)
 2	
 3	This project demonstrates how to use PostgreSQL as a message queue, implementing two different approaches:
 4	
 5	1. **Outbox Pattern**: A reliable way to implement eventual consistency in distributed systems
 6	2. **Native PostgreSQL Queue**: Utilizing PostgreSQL's LISTEN/NOTIFY, advisory locks, and other features
 7	
 8	## Features
 9	
 10	- Thread-safe implementations
 11	- SOLID design principles
 12	- Configurable retry mechanisms
 13	- Real-time notifications with LISTEN/NOTIFY
 14	- Optimistic locking for concurrency control
 15	- Connection pooling with HikariCP
 16	- Comprehensive error handling
 17

 776	public class TopicRouter<T> {
 777	 private final Map<String, List<Consumer<OutboxMessage<T>>>> topicHandlers = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
 778	 
 779	 public void registerHandler(String topic, Consumer<OutboxMessage<T>> handler) {
 780	 topicHandlers.computeIfAbsent(topic, k -> new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>()).add(handler);
 781	 }
 782	 
 783	 public void routeMessage(OutboxMessage<T> message, String topic) {
 784	 List<Consumer<OutboxMessage<T>>> handlers = topicHandlers.get(topic);
 785	 if (handlers != null && !handlers.isEmpty()) {
 786	 for (Consumer<OutboxMessage<T>> handler : handlers) {
 787	 try {
 788	 handler.accept(message);
 789	 } catch (Exception e) {
 790	 // Log error but continue with other handlers
 791	 }
 792	 }
 793	 }
 794	 }
 795	}

IF MORE CONTENT NEEDS TO BE ADDED USE THE str-replace-editor TOOL TO EDIT THE FILE AFTER IT HAS BEEN CREATED.", "path": "ADVANCED_GUIDE.md", "file_content": "# PeeGeeQ Advanced Guide: High-Frequency Messaging & Consumer Groups\n#### © Mark Andrew Ray-Smith Cityline Ltd 2025\n\nThis guide demonstrates advanced PeeGeeQ patterns for high-throughput scenarios, including high-frequency producers, multiple consumers, consumer groups, and message routing based on header keys.\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\n```mermaid\ngraph TB\n subgraph \"High-Frequency Producers\"\n HP1[Order Producer<br/>10,000 msg/sec]\n HP2[Payment Producer<br/>8,000 msg/sec]\n HP3[Inventory Producer<br/>5,000 msg/sec]\n end\n\n subgraph \"Message Router\"\n ROUTER[Header-Based Router<br/>Routes by: region, priority, type]\n end\n\n subgraph \"Consumer Groups\"\n subgraph \"Order Processing Group\"\n OC1[Order Consumer 1<br/>region=US]\n OC2[Order Consumer 2<br/>region=EU]\n OC3[Order Consumer 3<br/>region=ASIA]\n end\n \n subgraph \"Payment Processing Group\"\n PC1[Payment Consumer 1<br/>priority=HIGH]\n PC2[Payment Consumer 2<br/>priority=NORMAL]\n end\n \n subgraph \"Analytics Group\"\n AC1[Analytics Consumer 1<br/>All Messages]\n AC2[Analytics Consumer 2<br/>Backup]\n end\n end\n\n subgraph \"PeeGeeQ Native Queue\"\n QUEUE[(PostgreSQL<br/>queue_messages<br/>LISTEN/NOTIFY<br/>Advisory Locks)]\n end\n\n HP1 --> ROUTER\n HP2 --> ROUTER\n HP3 --> ROUTER\n ROUTER --> QUEUE\n QUEUE --> OC1\n QUEUE --> OC2\n QUEUE --> OC3\n QUEUE --> PC1\n QUEUE --> PC2\n QUEUE --> AC1\n QUEUE --> AC2\n```\n\n## High-Frequency Producer Implementation\n\n### 1. Optimized Producer Configuration\n\nFirst, create a high-performance configuration:\n\n```properties\n# High-Performance Configuration (peegeeq-highperf.properties)\n# Database Connection Pool - Optimized for high throughput\npeegeeq.database.pool.min-size=20\npeegeeq.database.pool.max-size=50\npeegeeq.database.pool.connection-timeout-ms=5000\npeegeeq.database.pool.idle-timeout-ms=300000\n\n# Performance Settings\npeegeeq.performance.async.enabled=true\npeegeeq.performance.async.thread-pool-size=30\npeegeeq.performance.batch.enabled=true\npeegeeq.performance.batch.max-size=500\npeegeeq.performance.batch.timeout=PT2S\n\n# Queue Settings for High Throughput\npeegeeq.queue.visibility-timeout=PT15S\npeegeeq.queue.max-retries=2\npeegeeq.queue.batch-size=50\n\n# Metrics and Monitoring\npeegeeq.metrics.enabled=true\npeegeeq.metrics.reporting-interval=PT30S\npeegeeq.circuit-breaker.enabled=true\npeegeeq.circuit-breaker.failure-threshold=10\n```\n\n### 2. High-Frequency Producer Class\n\n```java\npackage com.example.advanced;\n\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.api.*;\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.db.PeeGeeQManager;\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.db.config.PeeGeeQConfiguration;\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.db.provider.PgDatabaseService;\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.db.provider.PgQueueFactoryProvider;\nimport io.micrometer.core.instrument.MeterRegistry;\nimport io.micrometer.core.instrument.simple.SimpleMeterRegistry;\n\nimport java.util.Map;\nimport java.util.concurrent.*;\nimport java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;\n\npublic class HighFrequencyProducer {\n private final MessageProducer<OrderEvent> producer;\n private final ExecutorService executorService;\n private final AtomicLong messageCounter = new AtomicLong(0);\n private final MeterRegistry meterRegistry;\n \n public HighFrequencyProducer(PeeGeeQManager manager) throws Exception {\n // Create database service and factory\n DatabaseService databaseService = new PgDatabaseService(manager);\n QueueFactoryProvider provider = new PgQueueFactoryProvider();\n QueueFactory nativeFactory = provider.createNativeQueueFactory(databaseService);\n \n // Create producer for high-frequency messaging\n this.producer = nativeFactory.createProducer(\"order-events\", OrderEvent.class);\n \n // Create thread pool for concurrent message sending\n this.executorService = Executors.newFixedThreadPool(20);\n this.meterRegistry = new SimpleMeterRegistry();\n }\n \n /**\n * Sends messages at high frequency with different routing headers\n */\n public void startHighFrequencyProduction(int messagesPerSecond, int durationSeconds) {\n System.out.println(\"Starting high-frequency production: \" + messagesPerSecond + \" msg/sec for \" + durationSeconds + \" seconds\");\n \n ScheduledExecutorService scheduler = Executors.newScheduledThreadPool(5);\n \n // Calculate delay between messages\n long delayMicros = 1_000_000 / messagesPerSecond;\n \n scheduler.scheduleAtFixedRate(() -> {\n // Send batch of messages concurrently\n for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {\n executorService.submit(this::sendRoutedMessage);\n }\n }, 0, delayMicros / 10, TimeUnit.MICROSECONDS);\n \n // Stop after duration\n scheduler.schedule(() -> {\n scheduler.shutdown();\n System.out.println(\"Sent \" + messageCounter.get() + \" messages\");\n }, durationSeconds, TimeUnit.SECONDS);\n }\n \n private void sendRoutedMessage() {\n try {\n long msgId = messageCounter.incrementAndGet();\n \n // Create order event with routing information\n OrderEvent event = new OrderEvent(\n \"ORDER-\" + msgId,\n \"CREATED\",\n msgId % 1000 + 100.0, // Random amount\n \"customer-\" + (msgId % 10000)\n );\n \n // Create routing headers based on message characteristics\n Map<String, String> headers = createRoutingHeaders(msgId);\n \n // Send with correlation ID and message group for ordering\n String correlationId = \"corr-\" + msgId;\n String messageGroup = headers.get(\"region\") + \"-\" + headers.get(\"priority\");\n \n producer.send(event, headers, correlationId, messageGroup)\n .whenComplete((result, error) -> {\n if (error != null) {\n System.err.println(\"Failed to send message \" + msgId + \": \" + error.getMessage());\n }\n });\n \n } catch (Exception e) {\n System.err.println(\"Error creating message: \" + e.getMessage());\n }\n }\n \n private Map<String, String> createRoutingHeaders(long messageId) {\n // Distribute messages across regions\n String region = switch ((int)(messageId % 3)) {\n case 0 -> \"US\";\n case 1 -> \"EU\";\n case 2 -> \"ASIA\";\n default -> \"US\";\n };\n \n // Assign priority based on message characteristics\n String priority = (messageId % 10 < 2) ? \"HIGH\" : \"NORMAL\";\n \n // Message type for routing\n String type = (messageId % 5 == 0) ? \"PREMIUM\" : \"STANDARD\";\n \n return Map.of(\n \"region\", region,\n \"priority\", priority,\n \"type\", type,\n \"source\", \"order-service\",\n \"version\", \"2.0\",\n \"timestamp\", String.valueOf(System.currentTimeMillis())\n );\n }\n \n public void close() {\n executorService.shutdown();\n producer.close();\n }\n}\n```\n\n## Consumer Groups Implementation\n\n### 1. Header-Based Message Router\n\n```java\npackage com.example.advanced;\n\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.api.Message;\nimport java.util.Map;\nimport java.util.function.Predicate;\n\npublic class MessageRouter {\n \n /**\n * Creates a filter for messages based on header values\n */\n public static <T> Predicate<Message<T>> createHeaderFilter(String headerKey, String expectedValue) {\n return message -> {\n Map<String, String> headers = message.getHeaders();\n return headers != null && expectedValue.equals(headers.get(headerKey));\n };\n }\n \n /**\n * Creates a filter for multiple header conditions (AND logic)\n */\n public static <T> Predicate<Message<T>> createMultiHeaderFilter(Map<String, String> requiredHeaders) {\n return message -> {\n Map<String, String> headers = message.getHeaders();\n if (headers == null) return false;\n \n return requiredHeaders.entrySet().stream()\n .allMatch(entry -> entry.getValue().equals(headers.get(entry.getKey())));\n };\n }\n \n /**\n * Creates a priority-based filter\n */\n public static <T> Predicate<Message<T>> createPriorityFilter(String minPriority) {\n return message -> {\n Map<String, String> headers = message.getHeaders();\n if (headers == null) return false;\n \n String priority = headers.get(\"priority\");\n if (\"HIGH\".equals(minPriority)) {\n return \"HIGH\".equals(priority);\n } else if (\"NORMAL\".equals(minPriority)) {\n return \"HIGH\".equals(priority) || \"NORMAL\".equals(priority);\n }\n return true;\n };\n }\n}\n```\n\n### 2. Consumer Group Implementation\n\n```java\npackage com.example.advanced;\n\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.api.*;\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.db.PeeGeeQManager;\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.db.provider.PgDatabaseService;\nimport dev.mars.peegeeq.db.provider.PgQueueFactoryProvider;\n\nimport java.util.Map;\nimport java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture;\nimport java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicLong;\nimport java.util.function.Predicate;\n\npublic class ConsumerGroup {\n private final String groupName;\n private final MessageConsumer<OrderEvent> consumer;\n private final Predicate<Message<OrderEvent>> messageFilter;\n private final AtomicLong processedCount = new AtomicLong(0);\n private final String consumerId;\n \n public ConsumerGroup(String groupName, String consumerId, \n PeeGeeQManager manager, \n Predicate<Message<OrderEvent>> messageFilter) throws Exception {\n this.groupName = groupName;\n this.consumerId = consumerId;\n this.messageFilter = messageFilter;\n \n // Create consumer\n DatabaseService databaseService = new PgDatabaseService(manager);\n QueueFactoryProvider provider = new PgQueueFactoryProvider();\n QueueFactory nativeFactory = provider.createNativeQueueFactory(databaseService);\n \n this.consumer = nativeFactory.createConsumer(\"order-events\", OrderEvent.class);\n }\n \n public void startConsuming() {\n System.out.println(\"Starting consumer group: \" + groupName + \", consumer: \" + consumerId);\n \n consumer.subscribe(message -> {\n // Apply message filter\n if (!messageFilter.test(message)) {\n // Skip this message - it doesn't match our filter\n return CompletableFuture.completedFuture(null);\n }\n \n return processMessage(message);\n });\n }\n \n private CompletableFuture<Void> processMessage(Message<OrderEvent> message) {\n return CompletableFuture.supplyAsync(() -> {\n try {\n OrderEvent event = message.getPayload();\n Map<String, String> headers = message.getHeaders();\n \n // Simulate processing time based on priority\n int processingTime = \"HIGH\".equals(headers.get(\"priority\")) ? 50 : 200;\n Thread.sleep(processingTime);\n \n long count = processedCount.incrementAndGet();\n \n System.out.printf(\"[%s-%s] Processed message %s: %s (region=%s, priority=%s) [%d total]%n\",\n groupName, consumerId, message.getId(), event.getOrderId(),\n headers.get(\"region\"), headers.get(\"priority\"), count);\n \n return null;\n \n } catch (Exception e) {\n System.err.printf(\"[%s-%s] Error processing message %s: %s%n\",\n groupName, consumerId, message.getId(), e.getMessage());\n throw new RuntimeException(e);\n }\n });\n }\n \n public long getProcessedCount() {\n return processedCount.get();\n }\n \n public void stop() {\n consumer.unsubscribe();\n consumer.close();\n System.out.println(\"Stopped consumer group: \" + groupName + \", consumer: \" + consumerId);\n }\n}\n```\n\n## Complete Advanced Example\n\n### 1. Order Event Data Class\n\n```java\npackage com.example.advanced;\n\npublic class OrderEvent {\n private String orderId;\n private String status;\n private Double amount;\n private String customerId;\n \n // Constructors\n public OrderEvent() {}\n \n public OrderEvent(String orderId, String status, Double amount, String customerId) {\n this.orderId = orderId;\n this.status = status;\n this.amount = amount;\n this.customerId = customerId;\n }\n \n // Getters and setters\n public String getOrderId() { return orderId; }\n public void setOrderId(String orderId) { this.orderId = orderId; }\n \n public String getStatus() { return status; }\n public void setStatus(String status) { this.status = status; }\n \n public Double getAmount() { return amount; }\n public void setAmount(Double amount) { this.amount = amount; }\n \n public String getCustomerId() { return customerId; }\n public void setCustomerId(String customerId) { this.customerId = customerId; }\n \n @Override\n public String toString() {\n return String.format(\"OrderEvent{orderId='%s', status='%s', amount=%.2f, customerId='%s'}\", \n orderId, status, amount, customerId);\n }\n}\n```"}","mcp_server_name":"","mcp_tool_name":""}},{"id":2,"type":0,"content":"Now I have a comprehensive understanding of PeeGeeQ's capabilities.  1	# PeeGeeQ Examples
 2	
 3	This module contains self-contained example applications demonstrating PeeGeeQ's production readiness features.
 4	
 5	## Quick Start - Self-Contained Demo
 6	
 7	**For the easiest experience, use the self-contained demo:**
 8	
 9	```bash
 10	# Run the self-contained demo (requires Docker) - Recommended approach
 11	mvn compile exec:java -Dexec.mainClass="dev.mars.peegeeq.examples.PeeGeeQSelfContainedDemo" -pl peegeeq-examples
 12	
 13	# Alternative: Run directly with classpath
 14	java -cp "target/classes:..." dev.mars.peegeeq.examples.PeeGeeQSelfContainedDemo
 15	```
 16	
 17	This demo:
 18	- ✅ **No setup required** - starts its own PostgreSQL container
 19	- ✅ **Works out of the box** - no external dependencies
 20	- ✅ **Self-cleaning** - automatically removes containers when done
 21	- ✅ **Production-like** - uses real PostgreSQL database
 22	
 23	## Traditional Example
 24	
 25	**For testing with your own PostgreSQL setup:**
 26	
 27	```bash
 28	# Run with default development profile
 29	java -cp <classpath> dev.mars.peegeeq.examples.PeeGeeQExample
 30	
 31	# Run with specific profile
 32	java -Dpeegeeq.profile=production -cp <classpath> dev.mars.peegeeq.examples.PeeGeeQExample
...
 131	
 132	# If Docker is not running, start it:
 133	# - On Windows: Start Docker Desktop
 134	# - On macOS: Start Docker Desktop
 135	# - On Linux: sudo systemctl start docker
 136	```
 137	
 138	## Troubleshooting
 139	
 140	### Common Issues
 141	
 142	1. **Database Connection Failed**
 143	 - Verify PostgreSQL is running
 144	 - Check host, port, and credentials
 145	 - Ensure database exists and user has permissions
 146	
 147	2. **Docker Issues (Self-Contained Demo)**
 148	 - Ensure Docker is installed and running
 149	 - Check internet connectivity for image download
 150	 - Verify Docker has sufficient resources
 151	
 152	3. **Configuration Issues**
 153	 - Check system properties and environment variables
 154	 - Verify profile-specific configuration files
 155	 - Review logs for detailed error messages

 18	peegeeq.database.pool.max-lifetime-ms=1800000
 19	peegeeq.database.pool.auto-commit=true

 1	# PostgreSQL as a Message Queue (PeeGeeQ)
 2	
 3	This project demonstrates how to use PostgreSQL as a message queue, implementing two different approaches:
 4	
 5	1. **Outbox Pattern**: A reliable way to implement eventual consistency in distributed systems
 6	2. **Native PostgreSQL Queue**: Utilizing PostgreSQL's LISTEN/NOTIFY, advisory locks, and other features
 7	
 8	## Features
 9	
 10	- Thread-safe implementations
 11	- SOLID design principles
 12	- Configurable retry mechanisms
 13	- Real-time notifications with LISTEN/NOTIFY
 14	- Optimistic locking for concurrency control
 15	- Connection pooling with HikariCP
 16	- Comprehensive error handling
 17	
 18	## Architecture
 19	
 20	The project is organized into the following packages:
 21	
 22	```
 23	dev.mars.peegeeq
 24	├── api # Public interfaces
 25	│ ├── MessageQueue.java # Core queue interface
 26	│ ├── Message.java # Message interface
 27	│ └── Consumer.java # Message consumer interface
 28	├── core # Core implementations
 29	│ ├── PostgresConfig.java # Database configuration
 30	│ └── AbstractQueue.java # Common queue functionality
 31	├── outbox # Outbox pattern implementation
 32	│ ├── OutboxQueue.java # Outbox pattern queue
 33	│ └── OutboxMessage.java # Outbox message implementation
 34	├── pg # Native PostgreSQL queue implementation
 35	│ ├── PgQueue.java # Native PostgreSQL queue
 36	│ ├── PgMessage.java # Native queue message implementation
 37	│ └── NotificationListener.java # LISTEN/NOTIFY handler
 38	└── util # Utilities
 39	 ├── ConnectionPool.java # Thread-safe connection pool
 40	 └── ThreadSafetyUtils.java # Thread safety utilities
 41	```

 1	# PeeGeeQ - Getting Started Guide 
 2	#### © Mark Andrew Ray-Smith Cityline Ltd 2025
 3	
 4	Welcome to **PeeGeeQ** (PostgreSQL as a Message Queue) - a production-ready message queue system built on PostgreSQL that provides both high-performance real-time messaging and transactional messaging patterns.
 5	
 6	## What is PeeGeeQ?
 7	
 8	PeeGeeQ is an enterprise-grade message queue system that leverages PostgreSQL's advanced features to provide:
 9	
 10	- **Native Queue**: High-performance, real-time message processing (10,000+ msg/sec, <10ms latency)
 11	- **Outbox Pattern**: Transactional messaging with database consistency guarantees (5,000+ msg/sec)
 12	- **Production Features**: Health checks, metrics, circuit breakers, dead letter queues, and more
 13

 147	## Basic Usage
 148	
 149	### Initialize PeeGeeQ Manager
 150	
 151	```java
 152	import dev.mars.peegeeq.db.PeeGeeQManager;
 153	import dev.mars.peegeeq.db.config.PeeGeeQConfiguration;
 154	import io.micrometer.core.instrument.simple.SimpleMeterRegistry;
 155	
 156	// Initialize with configuration profile
 157	PeeGeeQManager manager = new PeeGeeQManager(
 158	 new PeeGeeQConfiguration("development"), 
 159	 new SimpleMeterRegistry()
 160	);
 161	
 162	// Start all services
 163	manager.start();
 164	```
 165	
 166	### Native Queue - High Performance Real-time
 167	
 168	```java
 169	import dev.mars.peegeeq.api.*;
 170	import dev.mars.peegeeq.db.provider.PgDatabaseService;
 171	import dev.mars.peegeeq.db.provider.PgQueueFactoryProvider;
 172	
 173	// Create database service and factory provider
 174	DatabaseService databaseService = new PgDatabaseService(manager);
 175	QueueFactoryProvider provider = new PgQueueFactoryProvider();
 176	
 177	// Create native queue factory
 178	QueueFactory nativeFactory = provider.createNativeQueueFactory(databaseService);
 179	
 180	// Create producer and consumer
 181	MessageProducer<String> producer = nativeFactory.createProducer("my-topic", String.class);
 182	MessageConsumer<String> consumer = nativeFactory.createConsumer("my-topic", String.class);
 183	
 184	// Send messages
 185	producer.send("Hello, PeeGeeQ!");
 186	
 187	// Consume messages
 188	consumer.consume(message -> {
 189	 System.out.println("Received: " + message.getPayload());
 190	 return true; // Acknowledge message
 191	});
 192	```
 193	
 194	### Outbox Pattern - Transactional Guarantees
 195	
 196	```java
 197	// Create outbox queue factory
 198	QueueFactory outboxFactory = provider.createOutboxQueueFactory(databaseService);
 199	
 200	// Create producer and consumer
 201	MessageProducer<String> outboxProducer = outboxFactory.createProducer("my-outbox-topic", String.class);
 202	MessageConsumer<String> outboxConsumer = outboxFactory.createConsumer("my-outbox-topic", String.class);
 203	
 204	// Send messages with transactional guarantees
 205	outboxProducer.send("Transactional message");
 206	
 207	// Consume messages
 208	outboxConsumer.consume(message -> {
 209	 System.out.println("Received transactional: " + message.getPayload());
 210	 return true;
 211	});
 212	```

 216	### Environment Profiles
 217	
 218	PeeGeeQ supports multiple configuration profiles:
 219	
 220	- `development` - Default settings for local development
 221	- `production` - Optimized for production environments
 222	- `test` - Configured for testing scenarios
 223	
 224	### Configuration Files
 225	
 226	Configuration is loaded from:
 227	1. `peegeeq-default.properties` (base configuration)

 229	3. System properties (highest priority)
 230	4. Environment variables

 169	
 170	The Native Queue implementation provides high-performance, real-time message processing using PostgreSQL's LISTEN/NOTIFY mechanism.
 171

 173

 175	
 176	```java
 177	// Using the unified factory pattern (recommended)
 178	DatabaseService databaseService = new PgDatabaseService(manager);
 179	QueueFactoryProvider provider = new PgQueueFactoryProvider();
 180	QueueFactory nativeFactory = provider.createFactory("native", databaseService);

 200	```

 202	### Sending Messages
 203	
 204	```java
 205	// Simple message
 206	producer.send("Order #12345 created").join();
 207	
 208	// Message with headers
 209	Map<String, String> headers = Map.of(
 210	 "source", "order-service",
 211	 "version", "1.0"
 212	);
 213	producer.send("Order #12346 created", headers).join();
 214	
 215	// Message with correlation ID
 216	producer.send("Order #12347 created", headers, "correlation-123").join();
 217	
 218	// Message with message group (for ordering)
 219	producer.send("Order #12348 created", headers, "correlation-124", "customer-456").join();
 220	```

 706	## Best Practices
 707	
 708	### When to Use Native Queue
 709	- High-throughput, low-latency requirements
 710	- Real-time event processing
 711	- Independent message processing
 712	- When immediate delivery is important
 713	
 714	### When to Use Outbox Pattern
 715	- Transactional consistency requirements
 716	- Integration with existing database transactions
 717	- When message delivery must be guaranteed
 718	- Complex business transactions

 125	## Key Features
 126	
 127	### 1. Real-time Message Processing
 128	- **LISTEN/NOTIFY**: Immediate message delivery using PostgreSQL's pub/sub
 129	- **Zero Polling**: Messages are pushed to consumers instantly
 130	- **Channel Management**: Automatic channel subscription and cleanup
 131	
 132	### 2. Concurrency Control
 133	- **Advisory Locks**: Prevents duplicate message processing
 134	- **Visibility Timeout**: Automatic message release after timeout
 135	- **Lock Expiration**: Background cleanup of expired locks
 136	
 137	### 3. Reliability & Resilience
 138	- **Dead Letter Queue**: Failed messages moved to DLQ after retry limit
 139	- **Circuit Breakers**: Automatic failure detection and recovery
 140	- **Health Checks**: Continuous system health monitoring
 141	- **Backpressure**: Automatic load management
...
 160	
 161	### Latency
 162	- **Real-time Delivery**: <10ms with LISTEN/NOTIFY
 163	- **Polling-based**: 2-5 seconds (configurable)
 164	- **Processing Overhead**: <1ms per message
 165	
 166	### Scalability
 167	- **Horizontal Scaling**: Multiple consumer instances
 168	- **Vertical Scaling**: Leverages PostgreSQL performance
 169	- **Connection Pooling**: Efficient resource utilization

 773	### 2. Message Routing
 774	
 775	```java
 776	public class TopicRouter<T> {
 777	 private final Map<String, List<Consumer<OutboxMessage<T>>>> topicHandlers = new ConcurrentHashMap<>();
 778	 
 779	 public void registerHandler(String topic, Consumer<OutboxMessage<T>> handler) {
 780	 topicHandlers.computeIfAbsent(topic, k -> new CopyOnWriteArrayList<>()).add(handler);
 781	 }
 782	 
 783	 public void routeMessage(OutboxMessage<T> message, String topic) {
 784	 List<Consumer<OutboxMessage<T>>> handlers = topicHandlers.get(topic);
 785	 if (handlers != null && !handlers.isEmpty()) {
 786	 for (Consumer<OutboxMessage<T>> handler : handlers) {
 787	 try {
 788	 handler.accept(message);
 789	 } catch (Exception e) {
 790	 // Log error but continue with other handlers
 791	 }
 792	 }
 793	 }
 794	 }
 795	}

The PeeGeeQ system implements two different PostgreSQL-based queue implementations, each optimized for different use cases:

## 1. **Outbox Pattern Implementation** (`peegeeq-outbox`)
- **Throughput**: 5,000+ messages/second
- **Latency**: 2-5 seconds (configurable polling interval)
- **Reliability**: Exactly-once processing guarantees with ACID transactions
- **Use Case**: Transactional messaging with strong consistency guarantees

## 2. **Native PostgreSQL Queue Implementation** (`peegeeq-native`)
- **Throughput**: 10,000+ messages/second 
- **Latency**: <10ms with LISTEN/NOTIFY
- **Features**: Real-time processing using PostgreSQL's LISTEN/NOTIFY mechanism
- **Use Case**: High-performance, real-time message processing

Both implementations can be accessed through a unified factory pattern:

## Enhanced Schema for Bi-Temporal Log Store

<augment_code_snippet path="db/migration/V002__Create_Bitemporal_Log_Store.sql" mode="EDIT">
```sql
-- Bi-temporal append-only log store
CREATE TABLE bitemporal_log (
 id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
 event_id UUID NOT NULL DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
 event_type VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
 aggregate_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
 sequence_number BIGINT NOT NULL,
 
 -- Bi-temporal dimensions
 valid_time_start TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
 valid_time_end TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT 'infinity',
 transaction_time TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),
 
 -- Event data
 event_data JSONB NOT NULL,
 metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
 correlation_id VARCHAR(255),
 causation_id VARCHAR(255),
 
 -- Versioning
 version INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
 
 CONSTRAINT unique_aggregate_sequence UNIQUE (aggregate_id, sequence_number)
);

-- Indexes for efficient querying
CREATE INDEX idx_bitemporal_log_aggregate_sequence ON bitemporal_log(aggregate_id, sequence_number);
CREATE INDEX idx_bitemporal_log_event_type ON bitemporal_log(event_type);
CREATE INDEX idx_bitemporal_log_valid_time ON bitemporal_log(valid_time_start, valid_time_end);
CREATE INDEX idx_bitemporal_log_transaction_time ON bitemporal_log(transaction_time);
CREATE INDEX idx_bitemporal_log_correlation ON bitemporal_log(correlation_id);
```
</augment_code_snippet>

## Bi-Temporal Event Store Implementation

<augment_code_snippet path="peegeeq-outbox/src/main/java/dev/mars/peegeeq/outbox/BiTemporalEventStore.java" mode="EDIT">
```java
public class BiTemporalEventStore<T> {
 private final DataSource dataSource;
 private final ObjectMapper objectMapper;
 private final MessageProducer<T> realTimeProducer;
 
 public BiTemporalEventStore(DataSource dataSource, MessageProducer<T> realTimeProducer) {
 this.dataSource = dataSource;
 this.objectMapper = new ObjectMapper();
 this.realTimeProducer = realTimeProducer;
 }
 
 @Transactional
 public CompletableFuture<Void> appendEvent(String aggregateId, String eventType, 
 T eventData, Instant validTime) {
 return CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {
 try (Connection conn = dataSource.getConnection()) {
 // Get next sequence number
 long sequenceNumber = getNextSequenceNumber(conn, aggregateId);
 
 // Insert into bi-temporal log
 String sql = """
 INSERT INTO bitemporal_log 
 (aggregate_id, event_type, sequence_number, valid_time_start, event_data, metadata)
 VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?::jsonb, ?::jsonb)
 """;
 
 try (PreparedStatement stmt = conn.prepareStatement(sql)) {
 stmt.setString(1, aggregateId);
 stmt.setString(2, eventType);
 stmt.setLong(3, sequenceNumber);
 stmt.setTimestamp(4, Timestamp.from(validTime));
 stmt.setString(5, objectMapper.writeValueAsString(eventData));
 stmt.setString(6, "{}");
 stmt.executeUpdate();
 }
 
 // Send to real-time queue for immediate processing
 Map<String, String> headers = Map.of(
 "event-type", eventType,
 "aggregate-id", aggregateId,
 "sequence-number", String.valueOf(sequenceNumber)
 );
 
 realTimeProducer.send(eventData, headers, 
 UUID.randomUUID().toString(), aggregateId);
 
 } catch (Exception e) {
 throw new RuntimeException("Failed to append event", e);
 }
 });
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

## Real-Time Event Stream Consumer

<augment_code_snippet path="peegeeq-outbox/src/main/java/dev/mars/peegeeq/outbox/RealTimeEventConsumer.java" mode="EDIT">
```java
public class RealTimeEventConsumer<T> {
 private final MessageConsumer<T> consumer;
 private final List<EventHandler<T>> handlers = new ArrayList<>();
 
 public void addHandler(EventHandler<T> handler) {
 handlers.add(handler);
 }
 
 public void startRealTimeProcessing() {
 consumer.receive()
 .handler(message -> {
 String eventType = message.headers().get("event-type");
 String aggregateId = message.headers().get("aggregate-id");
 
 handlers.forEach(handler -> {
 try {
 handler.handle(eventType, aggregateId, message.body());
 message.ack();
 } catch (Exception e) {
 logger.error("Handler failed for event {}", eventType, e);
 message.nack();
 }
 });
 })
 .exceptionHandler(error -> 
 logger.error("Real-time processing error", error));
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

## Usage Example

<augment_code_snippet path="example-bitemporal-usage.java" mode="EDIT">
```java
// Setup bi-temporal event store
QueueFactory factory = provider.createFactory("outbox", databaseService);
MessageProducer<OrderEvent> producer = factory.createProducer("events", OrderEvent.class);
BiTemporalEventStore<OrderEvent> eventStore = new BiTemporalEventStore<>(dataSource, producer);

// Real-time processing
RealTimeEventConsumer<OrderEvent> realTimeConsumer = new RealTimeEventConsumer<>(
 factory.createConsumer("events", OrderEvent.class));
realTimeConsumer.addHandler(new OrderEventHandler());
realTimeConsumer.startRealTimeProcessing();

// Append events with bi-temporal tracking
OrderEvent orderCreated = new OrderEvent("ORDER_CREATED", orderId, orderData);
eventStore.appendEvent(orderId, "ORDER_CREATED", orderCreated, Instant.now());

// Historical queries
HistoricalQueryService queryService = new HistoricalQueryService(dataSource);
List<EventRecord> eventsAsOfYesterday = queryService.getEventsAsOf(orderId, yesterday);
List<EventRecord> timeline = queryService.getEventTimeline(orderId);
```
</augment_code_snippet>

This design gives you:
- **Append-only**: Events are never deleted, only new versions added
- **Bi-temporal**: Track both when events happened (valid time) and when they were recorded (transaction time)
- **Real-time**: Immediate processing via PeeGeeQ's LISTEN/NOTIFY
- **Historical**: Query any point-in-time view of your data
- **Type safety**: Strongly typed events with JSON storage flexibility

````java path=example-bitemporal-usage.java mode=EDIT
OrderEvent orderCreated = new OrderEvent("ORDER_CREATED", orderId, orderData);
eventStore.appendEvent(orderId, "ORDER_CREATED", orderCreated, Instant.now());

// Historical queries
HistoricalQueryService queryService = new HistoricalQueryService(dataSource);
List<EventRecord> eventsAsOfYesterday = queryService.getEventsAsOf(orderId, yesterday);
List<EventRecord> timeline = queryService.getEventTimeline(orderId);
````

This design gives you:
- **Append-only**: Events are never deleted, only new versions added
- **Bi-temporal**: Track both when events happened (valid time) and when they were recorded (transaction time)
- **Real-time**: Immediate processing via PeeGeeQ's LISTEN/NOTIFY
- **Historical**: Query any point-in-time view of your data
- **Type safety**: Strongly typed events with JSON storage flexibility

when the event was recorded in the system.\n * This represents the system time when the event was persisted.\n *\n * @return The transaction time timestamp\n */\n Instant getTransactionTime();\n \n /**\n * Gets the version number of this event.\n * Used for tracking event evolution and corrections.\n *\n * @return The event version\n */\n long getVersion();\n \n /**\n * Gets the ID of the previous version of this event, if any.\n * Used for tracking event corrections and updates.\n *\n * @return The previous version ID, or null if this is the first version\n */\n String getPreviousVersionId();\n \n /**\n * Gets the headers associated with the event.\n * Can contain metadata, correlation IDs, etc.\n *\n * @return The event headers\n */\n Map<String, String> getHeaders();\n \n /**\n * Gets the correlation ID for tracking related events.\n *\n * @return The correlation ID, or null if not set\n */\n String getCorrelationId();\n \n /**\n * Gets the aggregate ID that this event belongs to.\n * Used for grouping related events together.\n *\n * @return The aggregate ID, or null if not set\n */\n String getAggregateId();\n \n /**\n * Indicates whether this event is a correction of a previous event.\n *\n * @return true if this is a correction, false otherwise\n */\n boolean isCorrection();\n \n /**\n * Gets the reason for the correction, if this is a correction event.\n *\n * @return The correction reason, or null if not a correction\n */\n String getCorrectionReason();\n}", "old_str_start_line_number_1": 1, "old_str_end_line_number_1": 1}","mcp_server_name":"","mcp_tool_name":""}},{"id":2,"type":0,"content":"Perfect! Now I have a good understanding of the PeeGeeQ codebase. Let me create a detailed plan for implementing the bi-temporal log store.

## Plan for Bi-Temporal Log Store Implementation

Based on my analysis of the PeeGeeQ codebase, I'll create an append-only bi-temporal log store that integrates seamlessly with the existing architecture. Here's my detailed plan:

### **Core Components to Create:**

1. **New API Module Components** (`peegeeq-api`):
 - `BiTemporalEvent<T>` - Core event interface with bi-temporal properties
 - `EventStore<T>` - Main interface for the bi-temporal log store
 - `EventQuery` - Query interface for historical and real-time queries
 - `TemporalRange` - Time range specifications for queries

2. **New Database Schema** (`peegeeq-db`):
 - New migration script for bi-temporal event log table
 - Indexes for efficient temporal queries
 - Views for simplified querying

3. **New Implementation Module** (`peegeeq-bitemporal`):
 - `PgBiTemporalEventStore<T>` - PostgreSQL-based implementation
 - `BiTemporalEventProducer<T>` - Producer for publishing events
 - `BiTemporalEventConsumer<T>` - Consumer for real-time event processing
 - `HistoricalQueryEngine` - Engine for point-in-time queries

4. **Integration with Existing PeeGeeQ**:
 - Leverage existing LISTEN/NOTIFY for real-time processing
 - Use existing metrics and monitoring infrastructure
 - Integrate with existing health checks and circuit breakers

### **Key Features:**

- **Append-only**: Events are never deleted, only new versions added
- **Bi-temporal**: Track both valid time (when events happened) and transaction time (when recorded)
- **Real-time**: Immediate processing via PeeGeeQ's LISTEN/NOTIFY
- **Historical**: Query any point-in-time view of data
- **Type safety**: Strongly typed events with JSON storage flexibility

 3	
 4	## Overview of Current Implementation
 5	
 6	Your project currently uses Project Reactor (reactor-core) for handling concurrency and asynchronous operations. The main reactive components in your codebase are:
 7	
 8	1. `PgQueue` interface that defines methods returning `Mono<Void>` and `Flux<T>`
 9	2. Two implementations: `OutboxQueue` and `PgNativeQueue` that use reactor-core's reactive types
 10	
 11	## Why Migrate to Vert.x?
 12	
 13	Vert.x offers several advantages:
 14	
 15	- A complete toolkit for building reactive applications, not just a reactive library
 16	- Built-in support for PostgreSQL via the Vert.x PostgreSQL client
 17	- Event-driven architecture that works well with PostgreSQL's LISTEN/NOTIFY
 18	- Non-blocking I/O operations with a simple programming model
 19	- Polyglot support if you need to expand beyond Java in the future
 20

 24

 29	 <!-- Add Vert.x version property -->

 31	 <!-- Keep other properties -->
 32	</properties>
 33	
 34	<dependencyManagement>
 35	 <dependencies>
 36	 <!-- Replace reactor-core with Vert.x -->
 37	 <dependency>
 38	 <groupId>io.vertx</groupId>
 39	 <artifactId>vertx-core</artifactId>
 40	 <version>${vertx.version}</version>
 41	 </dependency>
 42	 <dependency>
 43	 <groupId>io.vertx</groupId>
 44	 <artifactId>vertx-pg-client</artifactId>
 45	 <version>${vertx.version}</version>
 46	 </dependency>

 48	 <groupId>io.vertx</groupId>
 49	 <artifactId>vertx-sql-client</artifactId>
 50	 <version>${vertx.version}</version>
 51	 </dependency>
 52	 <!-- Keep other dependencies -->
 53	 </dependencies>
 54	</dependencyManagement>

 468	
 469	1. **Reactive Types**:
 470	 - Reactor: `Mono<T>` (0-1 items) and `Flux<T>` (0-n items)
 471	 - Vert.x: `Future<T>` (0-1 items) and `ReadStream<T>` (0-n items)
 472	
 473	2. **Execution Model**:
 474	 - Reactor: Operator-based pipeline with backpressure
 475	 - Vert.x: Event loop with handlers and futures
 476	
 477	3. **Database Access**:
 478	 - Reactor: Often used with R2DBC for reactive database access
 479	 - Vert.x: Has its own reactive PostgreSQL client

 306	 private void applyMigration(MigrationScript migration, Connection conn) throws SQLException {

 310	 // Execute migration script
 311	 try (Statement stmt = conn.createStatement()) {
 312	 stmt.execute(migration.getContent());
 313	 }
 314	
 315	 // Record migration
 316	 String sql = "INSERT INTO schema_version (version, description, checksum) VALUES (?, ?, ?)";
 317	 try (PreparedStatement stmt = conn.prepareStatement(sql)) {
 318	 stmt.setString(1, migration.getVersion());
 319	 stmt.setString(2, migration.getDescription());
 320	 stmt.setString(3, migration.getChecksum());
 321	 stmt.executeUpdate();
 322	 }
 323	
 324	 conn.commit();
 325	 } catch (Exception e) {
 326	 conn.rollback();

- **Historical**: Query any point-in-time view of data
- **Type safety**: Strongly typed events with JSON storage flexibility

"peegeeq-db/src/main/resources/db/migration/V003__Create_BiTemporal_Event_Log.sql", "file_content": "-- PeeGeeQ Database Schema - Bi-Temporal Event Log\n-- Version: 1.1.0\n-- Description: Create bi-temporal event log table for append-only event sourcing\n\n-- Bi-temporal event log table\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bitemporal_event_log (\n -- Primary key and identity\n id BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY,\n event_id VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n event_type VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,\n \n -- Bi-temporal dimensions\n valid_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE NOT NULL,\n transaction_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW() NOT NULL,\n \n -- Event data\n payload JSONB NOT NULL,\n headers JSONB DEFAULT '{}',\n \n -- Versioning and corrections\n version BIGINT DEFAULT 1 NOT NULL,\n previous_version_id VARCHAR(255),\n is_correction BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE NOT NULL,\n correction_reason TEXT,\n \n -- Grouping and correlation\n correlation_id VARCHAR(255),\n aggregate_id VARCHAR(255),\n \n -- Metadata\n created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW() NOT NULL,\n \n -- Constraints\n CONSTRAINT chk_version_positive CHECK (version > 0),\n CONSTRAINT chk_correction_reason CHECK (\n (is_correction = FALSE AND correction_reason IS NULL) OR\n (is_correction = TRUE AND correction_reason IS NOT NULL)\n ),\n CONSTRAINT chk_previous_version CHECK (\n (version = 1 AND previous_version_id IS NULL) OR\n (version > 1 AND previous_version_id IS NOT NULL)\n )\n);\n\n-- Indexes for efficient querying\n\n-- Primary temporal indexes\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_valid_time \n ON bitemporal_event_log(valid_time);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_transaction_time \n ON bitemporal_event_log(transaction_time);\n\n-- Bi-temporal composite index for point-in-time queries\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_valid_transaction \n ON bitemporal_event_log(valid_time, transaction_time);\n\n-- Event identification and type indexes\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_event_id \n ON bitemporal_event_log(event_id);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_event_type \n ON bitemporal_event_log(event_type);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_event_type_valid_time \n ON bitemporal_event_log(event_type, valid_time);\n\n-- Grouping and correlation indexes\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_aggregate_id \n ON bitemporal_event_log(aggregate_id) WHERE aggregate_id IS NOT NULL;\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_correlation_id \n ON bitemporal_event_log(correlation_id) WHERE correlation_id IS NOT NULL;\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_aggregate_valid_time \n ON bitemporal_event_log(aggregate_id, valid_time) WHERE aggregate_id IS NOT NULL;\n\n-- Version and correction indexes\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_version \n ON bitemporal_event_log(event_id, version);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_corrections \n ON bitemporal_event_log(previous_version_id) WHERE previous_version_id IS NOT NULL;\n\n-- Performance index for latest events\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_latest_events \n ON bitemporal_event_log(event_type, transaction_time DESC) \n WHERE is_correction = FALSE;\n\n-- GIN index for JSONB payload queries\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_payload_gin \n ON bitemporal_event_log USING GIN(payload);\n\n-- GIN index for JSONB headers queries\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_bitemporal_headers_gin \n ON bitemporal_event_log USING GIN(headers);\n\n-- Views for common queries\n\n-- Current state view (latest version of each event as of now)\nCREATE OR REPLACE VIEW bitemporal_current_state AS\nSELECT DISTINCT ON (event_id) \n id, event_id, event_type, valid_time, transaction_time,\n payload, headers, version, previous_version_id,\n is_correction, correction_reason, correlation_id, aggregate_id, created_at\nFROM bitemporal_event_log\nWHERE transaction_time <= NOW()\nORDER BY event_id, transaction_time DESC;\n\n-- Latest events view (most recent events by valid time)\nCREATE OR REPLACE VIEW bitemporal_latest_events AS\nSELECT \n id, event_id, event_type, valid_time, transaction_time,\n payload, headers, version, previous_version_id,\n is_correction, correction_reason, correlation_id, aggregate_id, created_at\nFROM bitemporal_event_log\nWHERE transaction_time <= NOW()\nORDER BY valid_time DESC;\n\n-- Event statistics view\nCREATE OR REPLACE VIEW bitemporal_event_stats AS\nSELECT \n COUNT(*) as total_events,\n COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_correction = TRUE) as total_corrections,\n COUNT(DISTINCT event_type) as unique_event_types,\n COUNT(DISTINCT aggregate_id) as unique_aggregates,\n MIN(valid_time) as oldest_event_time,\n MAX(valid_time) as newest_event_time,\n MIN(transaction_time) as oldest_transaction_time,\n MAX(transaction_time) as newest_transaction_time\nFROM bitemporal_event_log;\n\n-- Event type statistics view\nCREATE OR REPLACE VIEW bitemporal_event_type_stats AS\nSELECT \n event_type,\n COUNT(*) as event_count,\n COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_correction = TRUE) as correction_count,\n COUNT(DISTINCT aggregate_id) as unique_aggregates,\n MIN(valid_time) as oldest_event_time,\n MAX(valid_time) as newest_event_time\nFROM bitemporal_event_log\nGROUP BY event_type\nORDER BY event_count DESC;\n\n-- Function to get events as of a specific point in time\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION get_events_as_of_time(\n as_of_valid_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW(),\n as_of_transaction_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE DEFAULT NOW()\n)\nRETURNS TABLE (\n id BIGINT,\n event_id VARCHAR(255),\n event_type VARCHAR(255),\n valid_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,\n transaction_time TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE,\n payload JSONB,\n headers JSONB,\n version BIGINT,\n previous_version_id VARCHAR(255),\n is_correction BOOLEAN,\n correction_reason TEXT,\n correlation_id VARCHAR(255),\n aggregate_id VARCHAR(255),\n created_at TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE\n) AS $$\nBEGIN\n RETURN QUERY\n SELECT DISTINCT ON (bel.event_id)\n bel.id, bel.event_id, bel.event_type, bel.valid_time, bel.transaction_time,\n bel.payload, bel.headers, bel.version, bel.previous_version_id,\n bel.is_correction, bel.correction_reason, bel.correlation_id, \n bel.aggregate_id, bel.created_at\n FROM bitemporal_event_log bel\n WHERE bel.valid_time <= as_of_valid_time\n AND bel.transaction_time <= as_of_transaction_time\n ORDER BY bel.event_id, bel.transaction_time DESC;\nEND;\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;\n\n-- Trigger function for NOTIFY on new events\nCREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION notify_bitemporal_event() RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$\nBEGIN\n -- Send notification with event details\n PERFORM pg_notify(\n 'bitemporal_events',\n json_build_object(\n 'event_id', NEW.event_id,\n 'event_type', NEW.event_type,\n 'aggregate_id', NEW.aggregate_id,\n 'correlation_id', NEW.correlation_id,\n 'is_correction', NEW.is_correction,\n 'transaction_time', extract(epoch from NEW.transaction_time)\n )::text\n );\n \n -- Send type-specific notification\n PERFORM pg_notify(\n 'bitemporal_events_' || NEW.event_type,\n json_build_object(\n 'event_id', NEW.event_id,\n 'aggregate_id', NEW.aggregate_id,\n 'correlation_id', NEW.correlation_id,\n 'is_correction', NEW.is_correction,\n 'transaction_time', extract(epoch from NEW.transaction_time)\n )::text\n );\n \n RETURN NEW;\nEND;\n$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;\n\n-- Create trigger for real-time notifications\nCREATE TRIGGER trigger_notify_bitemporal_event\n AFTER INSERT ON bitemporal_event_log\n FOR EACH ROW\n EXECUTE FUNCTION notify_bitemporal_event();\n\n-- Comments for documentation\nCOMMENT ON TABLE bitemporal_event_log IS 'Bi-temporal event log for append-only event sourcing with valid time and transaction time dimensions';\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN bitemporal_event_log.valid_time IS 'When the event actually happened in the real world (business time)';\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN bitemporal_event_log.transaction_time IS 'When the event was recorded in the system (system time)';\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN bitemporal_event_log.version IS 'Version number for tracking event evolution and corrections';\nCOMMENT ON COLUMN bitemporal_event_log.is_correction IS 'Indicates whether this event is a correction of a previous event';\nCOMMENT ON VIEW bitemporal_current_state IS 'Current state view showing latest version of each event as of now';\nCOMMENT ON FUNCTION get_events_as_of_time IS 'Function to query events as they existed at a specific point in bi-temporal time';"}","mcp_server_name":"","mcp_tool_name":""}},{"id":2,"type":0,"content":"Now let the BiTemporalEvent interface.\n * \n * This class is part of the PeeGeeQ message queue system, providing\n * production-ready PostgreSQL-based message queuing capabilities with\n * bi-temporal event sourcing support.\n * \n * @param <T> The type of event payload\n * @author Mark Andrew Ray-Smith Cityline Ltd\n * @since 2025-07-15\n * @version 1.0\n */\npublic class SimpleBiTemporalEvent<T> implements BiTemporalEvent<T> {\n \n private final String eventId;\n private final String eventType;\n private final T payload;\n private final Instant validTime;\n private final Instant transactionTime;\n private final long version;\n private final String previousVersionId;\n private final Map<String, String> headers;\n private final String correlationId;\n private final String aggregateId;\n private final boolean isCorrection;\n private final String correctionReason;\n \n /**\n * Creates a new SimpleBiTemporalEvent.\n *\n * @param eventId The unique event identifier\n * @param eventType The event type\n * @param payload The event payload\n * @param validTime When the event actually happened\n * @param transactionTime When the event was recorded\n * @param version The event version\n * @param previousVersionId The previous version ID (for corrections)\n * @param headers Event headers\n * @param correlationId Correlation ID\n * @param aggregateId Aggregate ID\n * @param isCorrection Whether this is a correction\n * @param correctionReason Reason for correction (if applicable)\n */\n public SimpleBiTemporalEvent(String eventId, String eventType, T payload, \n correctionReason) {\n this.eventId = Objects.requireNonNull(eventId, \"Event ID cannot be null\");\n this.eventType = Objects.requireNonNull(eventType, \"Event type cannot be null\");\n this.payload = Objects.requireNonNull(payload, \"Payload cannot be null\");\n this.validTime = Objects.requireNonNull(validTime, \"Valid time cannot be null\");\n this.transactionTime = Objects.requireNonNull(transactionTime, \"Transaction time cannot be null\");\n this.version = version;\n this.previousVersionId = previousVersionId;\n this.headers = headers != null ? Map.copyOf(headers) : Map.of();\n this.correlationId = correlationId;\n this.aggregateId = aggregateId;\n this.isCorrection = isCorrection;\n this.correctionReason = correctionReason;\n \n // Validation\n if (version <= 0) {\n throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"Version must be positive\");\n }\n if (isCorrection && correctionReason == null) {\n throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"Correction reason is required for correction events\");\n }\n if (!isCorrection && correctionReason != null) {\n throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"Correction reason should only be set for correction events\");\n }\n if (version == 1 && previousVersionId != null) {\n throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"First version cannot have a previous version ID\");\n }\n if (version > 1 && previousVersionId == null) {\n throw new IllegalArgumentException(\"Versions after 1 must have a previous version ID\");\n }\n }\n \n /**\n * Creates a new SimpleBiTemporalEvent with minimal parameters.\n *\n * @param eventId The unique event identifier\n * @param eventType The event type\n * @param payload The event payload\n * @param validTime When the event actually happened\n * @param transactionTime When the event was recorded\n */\n public SimpleBiTemporalEvent(String eventId, String eventType, T payload, \n Instant validTime, Instant transactionTime) {\n this(eventId, eventType, payload, validTime, transactionTime, 1L, null, \n Map.of(), null, null, false, null);\n }\n \n /**\n * Creates a new SimpleBiTemporalEvent with headers and correlation.\n *\n * @param eventId The unique event identifier\n * @param eventType The event type\n * @param payload The event payload\n * @param validTime When the event actually happened\n * @param transactionTime When the event was recorded\n * @param headers Event headers\n * @param correlationId Correlation ID\n * @param aggregateId Aggregate ID\n */\n public SimpleBiTemporalEvent(String eventId, String eventType, T payload, \n Instant validTime, Instant transactionTime,\n Map<String, String> headers, String correlationId, \n String aggregateId) {\n this(eventId, eventType, payload, validTime, transactionTime, 1L, null,\n headers, correlationId, aggregateId, false, null);\n }\n \n @Override\n public String getEventId() {\n return eventId;\n }\n \n @Override\n public String getEventType() {\n return eventType;\n }\n \n @Override\n public T getPayload() {\n return payload;\n }\n \n @Override\n public Instant getValidTime() {\n return validTime;\n }\n \n @Override\n public Instant getTransactionTime() {\n return transactionTime;\n }\n \n @Override\n public long getVersion() {\n return version;\n }\n \n @Override\n public String getPreviousVersionId() {\n return previousVersionId;\n }\n \n @Override\n public Map<String, String> getHeaders() {\n return headers;\n }\n \n @Override\n public String getCorrelationId() {\n return correlationId;\n }\n \n @Override\n public String getAggregateId() {\n return aggregateId;\n }\n \n @Override\n public boolean isCorrection() {\n return isCorrection;\n }\n \n @Override\n public String getCorrectionReason() {\n return correctionReason;\n }\n \n @Override\n public boolean equals(Object o) {\n if (this == o) return true;\n if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;\n SimpleBiTemporalEvent<?> that = (SimpleBiTemporalEvent<?>) o;\n return version == that.version &&\n isCorrection == that.isCorrection &&\n Objects.equals(eventId, that.eventId) &&\n Objects.equals(eventType, that.eventType) &&\n Objects.equals(payload, that.payload) &&\n Objects.equals(validTime, that.validTime) &&\n Objects.equals(transactionTime, that.transactionTime) &&\n Objects.equals(previousVersionId, that.previousVersionId) &&\n Objects.equals(headers, that.headers) &&\n Objects.equals(correlationId, that.correlationId) &&\n Objects.equals(aggregateId, that.aggregateId) &&\n Objects.equals(correctionReason, that.correctionReason);\n }\n \n @Override\n public int hashCode() {\n return Objects.hash(eventId, eventType, payload, validTime, transactionTime,\n version, previousVersionId, headers, correlationId, \n aggregateId, isCorrection, correctionReason);\n }\n \n @Override\n public String toString() {\n return \"SimpleBiTemporalEvent{\" +\n \"eventId='\" + eventId + '\\'' +\n \", eventType='\" + eventType + '\\'' +\n \", validTime=\" + validTime +\n \", transactionTime=\" + transactionTime +\n \", version=\" + version +\n \", previousVersionId='\" + previousVersionId + '\\'' +\n \", correlationId='\" + correlationId + '\\'' +\n \", aggregateId='\" + aggregateId + '\\'' +\n \", isCorrection=\" + isCorrection +\n \", correctionReason='\" + {\n \n private static final Logger logger = LoggerFactory.getLogger(BiTemporalEventStoreExample.class);\n \n /**\n * Example event payload representing an order.\n */\n public static class OrderEvent {\n private final String orderId;\n private final String customerId;\n private final BigDecimal amount;\n private final String status;\n \n @JsonCreator\n public OrderEvent(@JsonProperty(\"orderId\") this.customerId = customerId;\n this.amount = amount;\n this.status = status;\n }\n \n public String getOrderId() { return orderId; }\n public String getCustomerId() { return customerId; }\n public BigDecimal getAmount() { return amount; }\n public String getStatus() { return status; }\n \n @Override\n public boolean equals(Object o) {\n if (this == o) return true;\n if (o == null || getClass() != o.getClass()) return false;\n OrderEvent that = (OrderEvent) o;\n return Objects.equals(orderId, that.orderId) &&\n Objects.equals(customerId, that.customerId) &&\n Objects.equals(amount, that.amount) &&\n Objects.equals(status, that.status);\n }\n \n @Override\n public int hashCode() {\n return Objects.hash(orderId, customerId, amount, status);\n }\n \n @Override\n public String toString() {\n return \"OrderEvent{\" +\n \"orderId='\" + orderId + '\\'' +\n \", customerId='\" + customerId + '\\'' +\n \", amount=\" + amount +\n \", status='\" + status + '\\'' +\n '}';\n }\n }\n \n public static void main(String[] args) {\n logger.info(\"Starting Bi-Temporal Event Store Example\");\n \n // Start PostgreSQL container\n try (PostgreSQLContainer<?> postgres = new PostgreSQLContainer<>(\"postgres:15\")\n .withDatabaseName(\"peegeeq_test\")\n .withUsername(\"test\")\n .withPassword(\"test\")) {\n \n postgres.start();\n logger.info(\"PostgreSQL container started on port: {}\", postgres.getFirstMappedPort());\n \n // Configure PeeGeeQ\n PeeGeeQConfiguration config = new PeeGeeQConfiguration();\n config.setJdbcUrl(postgres.getJdbcUrl());\n \n } catch (Exception e) {\n logger.error(\"Error with PostgreSQL container: {}\", e.getMessage(), e);\n }\n \n logger.info(\"Bi-Temporal Event Store Example completed\");\n }\n \n private static CompletableFuture<Void> runBiTemporalExample(EventStore<OrderEvent> eventStore) {\n return CompletableFuture.runAsync(() -> {\n try {\n logger.info(\"=== Bi-Temporal Event Store Example ===\");\n \n // 1. Append initial events\n logger.info(\"\\n1. Appending initial events...\");\n \n Instant baseTime = Instant.now().minus(1, ChronoUnit.HOURS);\n \n OrderEvent order1 = new OrderEvent(\"ORDER-001\", \"CUST-123\", \n new BigDecimal(\"99.99\"), \"CREATED\");\n OrderEvent order2 = new OrderEvent(\"ORDER-002\", \"CUST-456\", \n new BigDecimal(\"149.99\"), \"CREATED\");\n \n BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent> event1 = eventStore.append(\n \"OrderCreated\", order1, baseTime,\n Map.of(\"source\", \"web\", \"region\", \"US\"),\n \"corr-001\", \"ORDER-001\"\n ).join();\n \n BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent> event2 = eventStore.append(\n \"OrderCreated\", order2, baseTime.plus(10, ChronoUnit.MINUTES),\n Map.of(\"source\", \"mobile\", \"region\", \"EU\"),\n \"corr-002\", \"ORDER-002\"\n ).join();\n \n logger.info(\"Created event 1: {}\", event1.getEventId());\n logger.info(\"Created event 2: {}\", event2.getEventId());\n \n // 2. Query all events\n logger.info(\"\\n2. Querying all events...\");\n \n List<BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent>> allEvents = eventStore.query(EventQuery.all()).join();\n logger.info(\"Found {} events:\", allEvents.size());\n for (BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent> event : allEvents) {\n logger.info(\" Event: {} - {} - {}\", \n event.getEventId(), event.getEventType(), event.getPayload());\n }\n \n // 3. Query by event type\n logger.info(\"\\n3. Querying by event type...\");\n \n List<BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent>> orderEvents = eventStore.query(\n EventQuery.forEventType(\"OrderCreated\")\n ).join();\n logger.info(\"Found {} OrderCreated events\", orderEvents.size());\n \n // 4. Query by aggregate\n logger.info(\"\\n4. Querying by aggregate...\");\n \n List<BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent>> order1Events = eventStore.query(\n EventQuery.forAggregate(\"ORDER-001\")\n ).join();\n logger.info(\"Found {} events for ORDER-001\", order1Events.size());\n \n // 5. Add a correction event\n logger.info(\"\\n5. Adding correction event...\");\n \n OrderEvent correctedOrder = new OrderEvent(\"ORDER-001\", \"CUST-123\", \n new BigDecimal(\"89.99\"), \"CREATED\");\n \n BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent> correctionEvent = eventStore.appendCorrection(\n event1.getEventId(), \"OrderCreated\", correctedOrder, baseTime,\n Map.of(\"source\", \"web\", \"region\", \"US\", \"corrected\", \"true\"),\n \"corr-001\", \"ORDER-001\", \"Price correction due to discount\"\n ).join();\n \n logger.info(\"Created correction event: {}\", correctionEvent.getEventId());\n \n // 6. Get all versions of an event\n logger.info(\"\\n6. Getting all versions of ORDER-001 event...\");\n \n List<BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent>> versions = eventStore.getAllVersions(event1.getEventId()).join();\n logger.info(\"Found {} versions:\", versions.size());\n for (BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent> version : versions) {\n logger.info(\" Version {}: {} - Correction: {}\", \n version.getVersion(), version.getPayload().getAmount(), \n version.isCorrection());\n }\n \n // 7. Point-in-time query (as of transaction time)\n logger.info(\"\\n7. Point-in-time query (before correction)...\");\n \n Instant beforeCorrection = correctionEvent.getTransactionTime().minus(1, ChronoUnit.SECONDS);\n BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent> eventBeforeCorrection = eventStore.getAsOfTransactionTime(\n event1.getEventId(), beforeCorrection\n ).join();\n \n if (eventBeforeCorrection != null) {\n logger.info(\"Event before correction: {} (amount: {})\", \n eventBeforeCorrection.getEventId(), \n eventBeforeCorrection.getPayload().getAmount());\n } else {\n logger.info(\"No event found before correction time\");\n }\n \n // 8. Temporal range query\n logger.info(\"\\n8. Temporal range query...\");\n \n Instant rangeStart = baseTime.minus(30, ChronoUnit.MINUTES);\n Instant rangeEnd = baseTime.plus(30, ChronoUnit.MINUTES);\n \n List<BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent>> rangeEvents = eventStore.query(\n EventQuery.builder()\n .validTimeRange(new TemporalRange(rangeStart, rangeEnd))\n .sortOrder(EventQuery.SortOrder.VALID_TIME_ASC)\n .build()\n ).join();\n \n logger.info(\"Found {} events in time range:\", rangeEvents.size());\n for (BiTemporalEvent<OrderEvent> event : rangeEvents) {\n logger.info(\" Event: {} at {}\", \n event.getPayload().getOrderId(), event.getValidTime());\n }\n \n // 9. Get statistics\n logger.info(\"\\n9. Getting event store statistics...\");\n \n EventStore.EventStoreStats stats = eventStore.getStats().join();\n logger.info(\"Event Store Statistics:\");\n logger.info(\" Total events: {}\", stats.getTotalEvents());\n logger.info(\" Total corrections: {}\", stats.getTotalCorrections());\n logger.info(\" Event counts by type: {}\", stats.getEventCountsByType());\n logger.info(\" Oldest event time: {}\", stats.getOldestEventTime());\n logger.info(\" Newest event time: {}\", stats.getNewestEventTime());\n logger.info(\" Storage size: {} bytes\", stats.getStorageSizeBytes());\n \n logger.info(\"\\n=== Bi-Temporal Event Store Example Completed Successfully ===\");\n \n } catch (Exception e) {\n logger.error(\"Error in bi-temporal example: {}\", e.getMessage(), e);\n throw new RuntimeException(e);\n }\n });\n }\n}"}","mcp_server_name":"","mcp_tool_name":""}},{"id":2,"type":0,"content":"Now let me create a comprehensive example that demonstrates how to use the bi-temporal event store:
